title: Every Committee Selected by the Droop Monroe Rule Satisfies Droop Justified Representation
abstract: Does every committee selected by the Droop Monroe rule satisfy the Droop justified representation axiom? In multiwinner voting with approval ballots, the Droop justified representation property requires that every voter group of size strictly greater than $n / (k + 1)$ that jointly approves a candidate contains at least one voter who approves a committee member. We answer this question affirmatively, extending the justified representation guarantee from Hare-valid Monroe assignments to Droop-valid Monroe assignments without any divisibility constraints. The proof proceeds by contradiction: assuming a violation by an optimal Droop-Monroe committee, an exchange argument swapping an assigned committee member for the jointly approved candidate produces a valid assignment whose Monroe score strictly exceeds that of the optimal assignment, yielding a contradiction. The theorem has been formalized and mechanically verified in Lean as `droop_monroe_satisfies_droop_jr`.
introduction:
In approval-based multiwinner voting, selecting a committee of size $k$ representing $n$ voters requires balancing collective preferences with proportional representation. A fundamental fairness guarantee is justified representation under the Droop quota, or Droop-JR, studied in arXiv:2508.00811 (Table 1). A committee $W$ of size $k$ satisfies Droop-JR if every group of voters $S$ whose cardinality satisfies $(k + 1) \cdot |S| > n$ and who jointly approve at least one candidate contains at least one voter approving a candidate in $W$.

The Monroe rule seeks an assignment of voters to committee members that maximizes the number of voters assigned to candidates they approve, subject to capacity bounds on the clusters assigned to each candidate. Under Hare-valid Monroe assignments, representation guarantees have been established. However, Table 1 of arXiv:2508.00811 considers whether the Droop-JR guarantee extends to committees selected under Droop-valid Monroe assignments. In particular, Droop-valid assignments allow unassigned voters corresponding to the remainder under the Droop quota, while capping each candidate's assigned group at the quota upper bound $\lfloor (n + k) / (k + 1) \rfloor$, without requiring $n$ to be divisible by $k$ or $k + 1$.

We prove that every size-$k$ committee selected by the Droop Monroe rule satisfies Droop-JR. This result answers the question positively for all numbers of voters $n$ and candidates $m$, without any divisibility constraints on $n$ and $k$.
result:
Let $n, m, k$ be natural numbers, and let $A : \mathrm{Fin}\; n \to \mathrm{Finset}\;(\mathrm{Fin}\; m)$ represent the approval ballots of $n$ voters over $m$ candidates. A committee $W \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\; m$ of size $k$ is a Droop-Monroe committee, formalized as `is_droop_monroe_committee`, if there exists a Droop-valid assignment $\pi$ for $W$ whose Monroe score (`droop_monroe_score`) is maximal among all Droop-valid assignments for all size-$k$ committees.

Theorem (`droop_monroe_satisfies_droop_jr`). Every committee $W$ of size $k$ selected by the Droop Monroe rule satisfies Droop-JR (`is_droop_jr`): for every voter subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\; n$ such that $|S| > n / (k + 1)$ and $\bigcap_{i \in S} A(i) \neq \emptyset$, there exists some voter $i \in S$ who approves at least one candidate in $W$, that is, $A(i) \cap W \neq \emptyset$.

The Lean statement universally quantifies over the voter and candidate counts $n, m : \mathbb{N}$, the approval profile $A : \mathrm{Fin}\; n \to \mathrm{Finset}\;(\mathrm{Fin}\; m)$, the target committee size $k : \mathbb{N}$, and the committee $W : \mathrm{Finset}\;(\mathrm{Fin}\; m)$, asserting without restrictions to small cases that `is_droop_monroe_committee A k W` implies `is_droop_jr A k W`.
proof:
The proof proceeds by contradiction. Let $W$ be a committee selected by the Droop Monroe rule (`is_droop_monroe_committee`), and let $\pi$ be a Droop-valid assignment for $W$ that attains maximal Monroe score (`droop_monroe_score`). Suppose that Droop-JR (`is_droop_jr`) fails: there exists a voter set $S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\; n$ with $(k + 1) \cdot |S| > n$ and a candidate $c$ such that $c \in A(i)$ for all $i \in S$, yet $A(i) \cap W = \emptyset$ for every $i \in S$.

First, because $(k + 1) \cdot |S| > n \ge 0$, the set $S$ has positive cardinality and is nonempty. Second, if $c \in W$, then every voter in $S$ would approve a candidate in $W$, which contradicts the assumption that Droop-JR is violated; thus $c \notin W$.

Third, since every candidate assigned under $\pi$ belongs to $W$ and no voter in $S$ approves any candidate in $W$, no voter in $S$ is assigned to an approved candidate under $\pi$.

Fourth, not all voters in $S$ can be unassigned under $\pi$. Under a valid Droop-Monroe assignment, the number of unassigned voters is exactly $\lfloor n / (k + 1) \rfloor$. If every voter in $S$ were unassigned, then $S$ would be a subset of the unassigned voters, implying $(k + 1) \cdot |S| \le (k + 1) \cdot \lfloor n / (k + 1) \rfloor \le n$, which contradicts $(k + 1) \cdot |S| > n$. Therefore, there exist a voter $i_0 \in S$ and a candidate $c_0 \in W$ such that $\pi(i_0) = c_0$.

We now apply the exchange lemma `droop_monroe_exchange`. Swapping $c_0 \in W$ for $c \notin W$ produces a valid assignment $\pi'$ for the committee $(W \setminus \{c_0\}) \cup \{c\}$ satisfying the score inequality:
$$\mathrm{score}(\pi) + \min(|R|, |S|) \le \mathrm{score}(\pi') + |R \setminus S|,$$
where $R = \{i \mid \pi(i) = c_0\}$ is the set of voters assigned to $c_0$ under $\pi$.

By the optimality of $W$ and $\pi$ under `is_droop_monroe_committee`, any valid assignment $\pi'$ satisfies $\mathrm{score}(\pi') \le \mathrm{score}(\pi)$.

Next, we evaluate $\min(|R|, |S|)$. The validity of $\pi$ enforces the upper quota constraint on $c_0 \in W$, namely $|R| \le \lfloor (n + k) / (k + 1) \rfloor$ (expressed in Lean as $(n + k) / (k + 1)$, representing $\lceil n / (k + 1) \rceil$). The condition $(k + 1) \cdot |S| > n$ implies $\lfloor n / (k + 1) \rfloor < |S|$ by integer division. Since $n + k \le n + k + 1$, we have:
$$\lfloor (n + k) / (k + 1) \rfloor \le \lfloor (n + k + 1) / (k + 1) \rfloor = \lfloor n / (k + 1) \rfloor + 1 \le |S|.$$
It follows that $|R| \le |S|$, so $\min(|R|, |S|) = |R|$.

Partitioning $R$ into disjoint sets gives $|R| = |R \setminus S| + |R \cap S|$. Because $i_0 \in S$ and $\pi(i_0) = c_0$, we have $i_0 \in R \cap S$, so $|R \cap S| > 0$.

Substituting into the exchange inequality gives:
$$\mathrm{score}(\pi) + |R \setminus S| + |R \cap S| \le \mathrm{score}(\pi') + |R \setminus S| \le \mathrm{score}(\pi) + |R \setminus S|,$$
which implies $|R \cap S| \le 0$. This contradicts $|R \cap S| > 0$, completing the proof.
discussion: The theorem `droop_monroe_satisfies_droop_jr` answers the question posed in Table 1 of arXiv:2508.00811, showing that every committee selected by the Droop Monroe rule satisfies Droop-JR. Earlier justified representation guarantees for the Monroe rule applied to Hare-valid assignments; this result extends Droop-JR to Droop-valid Monroe assignments in full generality, requiring no divisibility constraints on $n$ and $k$. The argument relies crucially on the quota bounds defining Droop validity—specifically that the cluster size satisfies $|R| \le \lfloor (n + k) / (k + 1) \rfloor \le |S|$, and that the number of unassigned voters is at most $\lfloor n / (k + 1) \rfloor < |S|$.
research: a new question answered: Extends the Droop-JR justified representation guarantee from Hare-valid Monroe assignments to Droop-valid Monroe assignments without any divisibility constraints.
